abstract: Ranking honeybee colonies according to multiple performance criteria is central to selection in bee breeding, but deterministic scores provide limited information about how a selected colony compares with the population of available colonies. We propose a population-calibrated probabilistic score based on a weighted Euclidean distance to an ideal colony and an estimation of the joint distribution of the data. For a candidate colony, the probability-score is the probability that a colony drawn from a reference population outperforms the candidate. We estimate the dependence structure among criteria using a vine copula after apiary-specific rank transformations, allowing different marginal distributions while modelling a common dependence structure. Importantly, the joint distribution calibrates the distance into a probability but does not change the ordering induced by a fixed distance and weight vector. We apply the method to 265 observations from eight French and Italian apiaries during the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Dependence among the four criteria is weak in this dataset, and the vine-copula and independence probability-scores are therefore similar. A simulation study evaluates probability-score estimation under a range of dependence structures, while bootstrap and apiary-subset analyses quantify sensitivity to sampling and study composition. We additionally assess preference robustness by evaluating the proportion of admissible weight vectors for which a colony belongs to the top ranking. The framework provides an interpretable and reproducible population-relative score for multi-criteria colony selection.
